subject: Control-path carveout and egress fabric review for Novara private VPC
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novara-sys.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: netops@novara-sys.com
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Novara private VPC - initial control/data plane constraints

Thanks for the walkthrough this morning. A few constraints from our side that should shape the design before we get into diagrams: 

- Control plane (management, config API) must not traverse tenant data paths; it needs a dedicated management VLAN and a bastion hop for operator access.
- All egress to third-party telemetry endpoints (SaaS metrics) must go through our centralized egress proxy cluster in the DMZ; we cannot allow direct outbound from runtime nodes.
- We require proof of key rotation paths for the control-plane certificates and evidence that audit logging reaches our SIEM without touching runtime traffic.

Can Redwood sketch a reference topology that: 1) isolates the control-plane management subnet, 2) shows how KV cache or model artifacts are pulled without exposing runtime VMs to the management plane, and 3) routes telemetry via our egress fabric?

Alex
Network Architect, Novara Systems

---
Attachment: requirements-20261216.pdf (list of constraints)
From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novara-sys.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 12:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Novara private VPC - initial control/data plane constraints

Alex — thanks, this is clear and very helpful. I sketched an initial reference and attached a Draw.io export (vpc_controlplane_carveout_v1.drawio) plus a short PDF that maps the requested constraints to our runtime components. High level notes below, then a couple of explicit asks for your NetOps team.

Summary of proposed pattern:
- Carve out a dedicated control-path subnet (CPS) reachable only from our control-plane bastion and Novara operator IPs. Management API endpoints (versioned model pinning, rollout control) will be hosted in CPS.
- Runtime nodes (data plane) live in tenant VPCs with no ingress from CPS; a unidirectional pull pattern will be used for artifacts (signed manifests over mTLS) initiated from the data plane to an authenticated artifact gateway in a staging subnet.
- Egress fabric: runtime nodes route outbound to Novara DMZ egress cluster. We add a lightweight sidecar that tunnels telemetry and logs to the egress proxy; only encrypted telemetry leaves the runtime subnets.

Actionable questions for Novara NetOps:
1) Can you confirm the preferred bastion model (static jump host IP vs. ephemeral sessions through SAML-brokered access)?
2) Any pre-existing IP allowlists for SIEM ingest endpoints we should include in the drawio?

I'll wait for NetOps feedback and then propose a BGP/ACL snippet for the egress fabric.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Network Ops <netops@novara-sys.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, alex.chen@novara-sys.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Novara private VPC - initial control/data plane constraints

Dylan / Alex — quick answers from NetOps: 

- Bastion: we prefer ephemeral sessions brokered by our IdP (SAML + OIDC short-lived certs). Static IP allowlists are available for outbound but we'd rather avoid static operator IPs for management access.
- SIEM: syslog and HTTPS ingestion endpoints are monitored; primary IP ranges are 34.198.0.0/18 and 34.199.0.0/18 (we'll confirm exact ranges).
- Egress: DMZ egress cluster will terminate TLS and perform DLP. We need visibility on the sidecar's cert rotation schedule so the proxy can accept rotated keys without manual sync.

We reviewed the drawio you attached — high-level looks fine but we have two requests: 
1) Show a control-plane ingress filter at the gateway (deny-by-default with explicit management CIDRs).
2) Annotate the artifact-pull path with expected ports and TLS termination points.

I'll open a short ticket JIRA-OPS-4127 to track the egress ACL confirmations and IP allowlist.

—NetOps
From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: netops@novara-sys.com, alex.chen@novara-sys.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Novara private VPC - initial control/data plane constraints

Thanks — this is great. I've updated the diagram per NetOps requests and attached:
- vpc_controlplane_carveout_v1.drawio (annotated with management CIDRs and bastion flow)
- egress_fabric_reference.pdf (BGP peering sketch + sample ACLs)
- example-bgp-acls.txt (example ACLs + port list)

Key confirmation items before we lock the design: 
- IdP brokered ephemeral bastion is acceptable (we will integrate SSO automation for short-lived certs).
- Novara to confirm final SIEM IP ranges; we will mark those as allowed egress from the proxy cluster only.
- We will implement an artifact gateway that uses mTLS mutual auth; runtime nodes initiate outbound pulls on port 8443.

Next steps / owners:
- NetOps (Novara): confirm SIEM IP ranges in JIRA-OPS-4127 and provide any additional DLP rules to mirror (due 2026-12-22).
- Redwood (Jonas): produce a final network ACL + BGP snippet for your review (target 2026-12-20).
- Redwood (Kimberly): prepare control-plane runbook pages for operator access and certificate rotation flow (target 2026-12-21).

If that timeline works I'll schedule a 45-minute follow-up on Monday to walk the final diagram and runbook.

Thanks all —
Dylan Brooks
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
